thread:
IncidentBot: ALERT: P95 CPU for runtime-tokenizer service >= 95% across cluster us-west-2 for 3m. paging: @oncall (Ryan) p99 latency spike detected. :rotating_light:
Ryan (oncall): I'm paged, looking. seeing pod restarts on nodes gke-cpupool-3-*. getting lots of `TokenizerWorker` CPU spin.
Alice M.: same, hundreds of prompt-processing jobs queued. dashboard: https://redwood/infradash/alerts/1769004321
Carla (SRE): sampling logs from pod runtime-tokenizer-7f8c9: `kworker: task killed as result of memory overcommit` then `OOMKilled` on container. also a few `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` in companion gpu-worker pods when they try to pick up fallbacks.
Ben S.: paste of top from the pod node (snipped):
```
PID USER      PR  NI    VIRT    RES    SHR S %CPU %MEM     TIME+ COMMAND
3124 tokenizer 20   0  12.3g  10.8g   300m R  98.7 45.1   12:34.12 TokenizerWorker
3140 tokenizer 20   0  11.9g  10.2g   220m R  92.3 42.8    8:51.03 TokenizerWorker
```
Liz: looks like a prompt-hotloop: malformed prompt triggers exponential backtrack in tokenizer regex, causing CPU blowup and memory growth. we've seen this pattern in synthetic fuzz tests but not at this scale.
Rohan: I can confirm logs show repeated regex backtrack frames: `re2::MaxRecursion` not reached but recursion depth high.
Ryan (oncall): immediate mitigation plan?
Alice M.: steps: 1) scale down concurrency on runtime-tokenizer HPA to 1 2) cordon node gke-cpupool-3-2 and drain pods 3) add a temporary admission webhook to block the problematic prompt signature (regex fingerprint) 4) rollback to model v2.14 which has a tokenizer-limiter patch.
Carla (SRE): I'm cordoning the node now: `kubectl cordon gke-cpupool-3-2` 5:02:13 UTC.
Carla (SRE): starting `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force gke-cpupool-3-2` moving pods. some pods are CrashLoopBackOff, drain taking longer.
Ben S.: applying HPA patch: `kubectl -n runtime patch hpa/runtime-tokenizer -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":1,"maxReplicas":1}}'` -- reduced concurrency.
IncidentBot: NOTE: Pager duty acknowledgement by Ryan at 5:03:01 UTC.
Ryan (oncall): adding temporary rate limit config to runtime: `tokenizer.max_tokens_per_request=250`, `tokenizer.concurrent_jobs=6` via rolling configmap patch.
Alice M.: pushing a small hotfix to block the regex path: gist link with patch snippet. rolling update to model router to route traffic to v2.14 for churn-sensitive customers.
Liz: customer impact: some customers on dedicated capacity saw token failures and 503s for ~4-7 minutes while autoscaling and cordon/evict happened. hosted API fallback to smaller model variants triggered some CUDA errors for GPU worker pods that tried to accept higher memory footprints and then hit invalid address — we rolled back GPU routing.
Rohan: posted a snippet of the container logs showing `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` after OOM followed by `containerd: container died, exit code 137`.
Ben S.: while draining I saw kubelet log `eviction threshold reached: memory.available` on node; kernel dmesg lines show `Out of memory: Kill process 3124 (TokenizerWorker) score 987 or sacrifice child`.
Ryan (oncall): created incident ticket: INC-2026-0456, paging SRE team for root cause follow-up.
Alice M.: long-term mitigation proposals here: 1) add guarded tokenizer mode with recursion depth limits 2) add prompt-length and tokenization complexity scoring at the edge (pre-accept) 3) run regex backtrack fuzzing in CI 4) per-tenant token caps and circuit breakers 5) failure mode fallback to pre-tokenized path if tokenizer CPU > 80%
Carla (SRE): I've uncordoned the node at 5:10:02 UTC after successful kubelet restart and OS reclaim on one host; but we're keeping it out of rotation until kernel OOM logs are cleared.
Ryan (oncall): handing off to SRE shift B (Carla) for deeper RCA. I'm going to sleep, will join for postmortem. cc @Carla (SRE) :zzz: Thanks all.
Carla (SRE): I'll collect logs and timeline. immediate customer-facing status update drafted: "We experienced a tokenizer processing spike causing CPU resource exhaustion and pod restarts; mitigations applied include concurrency limits, node cordon/drain, and rollback to a tokenizer-safe model variant. Root cause investigation in progress." Please add impact notes.
Ben S.: adding list of affected customer IDs to the ticket (internal); initial estimate: ~12 hosted customers saw 5xxs, 3 Dedicated customers saw degraded throughput for ~6 minutes.
Liz: following up with reproducer and small failing prompt sample pinned in the incident ticket. patch PR #2648 created to add regex guard.
IncidentBot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: CPU spike subsided, pods stable at 5:16:39 UTC. Final status: service recovered after HPA limits + model rollback.
Carla (SRE): marking actionable items, will schedule postmortem tomorrow 14:00 UTC.
Ryan (oncall): acknowledged handoff. thanks for quick responses. :thumbsup:
